claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys are governed by coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates relieve local stress concentrations that can initiate premature cracks.
A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy processed without tailored heat treatments has incoherent or absent nanoprecipitates.
Controlled heat treatment and compositional adjustment can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in the alloy.
Testing at approximately 800 °C is relevant to the elevated-temperature performance of tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
A controlled atmosphere at approximately 800 °C mimics a fusion plasma-facing environment.
Nanoprecipitate density and particle-matrix interfacial coherency are the structural mediators of the mechanical response.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate easier dislocation motion.
Coherent precipitate interfaces distribute local stresses more evenly and thereby delay crack nucleation.
SCCP-engineered samples will have significantly higher elevated-temperature plastic strain capacity than the baseline.
SCCP-engineered samples will have significantly higher elevated-temperature toughness than the baseline.
SCCP-engineered samples will exhibit delayed crack initiation and microstructural evidence of enhanced dislocation transmission.
Conventionally processed control samples will contain incoherent, minimal, or random precipitate features.
The mechanism should apply to tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys and similarly processed tungsten-based materials under high-temperature fusion-relevant conditions.
Grain boundaries and secondary phases may also influence high-temperature mechanical behavior.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in plastic strain, toughness, or crack-initiation delay in the SCCP samples would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes a compositional adjustment, while the conditions require alloy composition to be held constant. The proposed two-set experiment therefore cannot simultaneously vary composition as part of the intervention and isolate nanoprecipitate coherency with composition controlled.
